newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rheinelektra, Lahmeyer to merge into HfB Holding.
newsitem.headline: Rheinelektra, Lahmeyer to merge into HfB Holding.

text.p: German utilities Lahmeyer AG and Rheinelektra AG said in a mandatory statement on Wednesday that they had decided to merge into one company, HfB (Holding fuer Beteiligungswerte AG).

The companies are both over 60-percent owned by Essen-based RWE AG, one of Germany's biggest utility companies. Upon completion of the merger, the new company will be known as Lahmeyer AG, based in Frankfurt.

The companies said that Lahmeyer shareholders would receive 32 HfB shares and 49 pfennigs for every three shares, while Rheinelektra shareholders would receive 64 HfB shares and 34 pfennigs per share.
Rheinelektra, Lahmeyer to merge into HfB =2

The management boards of Lahmeyer and Rheinelektra will put the proposal forward for approval by shareholders at an extraordinary shareholders meeting to be held in Bad Homburg in Germany on February 25.
The move has been approved by the board of RWE, the statement said.
